answer: SELECT r.yr AS race_year, r.event_schedule->>'event_name' AS race_name, concat_ws(' ', d.driver_identity->'name'->>'first_name', d.driver_identity->'name'->>'surname') AS driver_name, (s.sprint_performance->>'final_position')::int AS podium_position, floor((to_date(r.event_schedule->>'date_set','YYYY/MM/DD') - (d.driver_identity->>'birth_date')::date)/365.25)::int AS age_at_race FROM sprint_results s JOIN races r ON r.rak_id = s.matchref JOIN drivers d ON d.drv_main = s.unitdrive WHERE (s.sprint_performance->>'final_position')::int BETWEEN 1 AND 3 AND floor((to_date(r.event_schedule->>'date_set','YYYY/MM/DD') - (d.driver_identity->>'birth_date')::date)/365.25) >= 35 ORDER BY age_at_race DESC, r.yr DESC
note: The only per-race classification table in this database is sprint_results (there is no main-race results table), so podiums are taken from sprint finishing positions.

answer: WITH s AS (SELECT cr.unitnode, COUNT(*) AS starts, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.st_mark IS NULL) AS finishes FROM constructor_results cr GROUP BY cr.unitnode) SELECT ROUND(MAX(finishes * 100.0 / starts), 2) AS max_reliability_rate FROM s WHERE starts >= 5

WITH s AS (SELECT c.cstr_key, c.namelabel AS constructor_name, COUNT(*) AS races_started, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.st_mark IS NULL) AS races_finished FROM constructor_results cr JOIN constructors c ON c.cstr_key = cr.unitnode GROUP BY c.cstr_key, c.namelabel) SELECT constructor_name, races_started, races_finished, ROUND(races_finished * 100.0 / races_started, 2) AS reliability_rate, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY races_finished * 100.0 / races_started DESC) AS reliability_rank FROM s WHERE races_started > 10 ORDER BY reliability_rate DESC

WITH per_race AS (SELECT wheel_unit, rc_index, STDDEV_POP(msec_val / 1000.0) AS ltc FROM lap_times GROUP BY wheel_unit, rc_index) SELECT jsonb_build_object('surname', d.driver_identity->'name'->>'surname', 'first_name', d.driver_identity->'name'->>'first_name') AS driver_name, AVG(p.ltc) AS avg_consistency_score, COUNT(*) AS races_analyzed FROM per_race p JOIN drivers d ON d.drv_main = p.wheel_unit GROUP BY d.drv_main, d.driver_identity HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY avg_consistency_score ASC

WITH h AS (SELECT drv_main, (driver_identity->>'birth_date')::date AS bd FROM drivers WHERE driver_identity->>'reference' = 'hamilton'), s AS (SELECT ds.rlink, ds.acc_pt, COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY ds.rlink) AS races_participated, h.bd FROM driver_standings ds JOIN h ON h.drv_main = ds.drive_link) SELECT rlink AS race_id, (acc_pt / races_participated) / floor((CURRENT_DATE - bd) / 365.25) AS dpv FROM s ORDER BY rlink
note: PPR taken as the cumulative points in driver_standings divided by the running count of Hamilton's standings rows; Driver Age uses the current date as the knowledge base defines it. Both choices are interpretations.

answer: SELECT ROUND(AVG((CASE WHEN q.px_pos = 1 THEN 0.35 ELSE 0.05 END) * (CASE WHEN q.px_pos = 1 THEN 0.25 ELSE 0.08 END)), 4) AS hat_trick_probability FROM qualifying q WHERE q.px_pos = 1
SELECT MIN(msec_val) / 1000.0 AS fastest_lap_seconds FROM lap_times WHERE msec_val > 0
WITH a AS (SELECT matchidx, COUNT(*)::numeric / COUNT(DISTINCT wunit) AS avg_stops_per_car FROM pit_stops GROUP BY matchidx) SELECT COUNT(*) AS single_stop_races FROM a WHERE avg_stops_per_car < 1.5

WITH w AS (SELECT matchref, (sprint_performance->'timing'->>'duration_ms')::bigint AS ms FROM sprint_results WHERE (sprint_performance->>'final_position')::int = 1), s AS (SELECT matchref, (sprint_performance->'timing'->>'duration_ms')::bigint AS ms FROM sprint_results WHERE (sprint_performance->>'final_position')::int = 2) SELECT COUNT(*) AS dominant_victories FROM w JOIN s ON s.matchref = w.matchref WHERE (s.ms - w.ms) / 1000.0 > 5

SELECT AVG(floor((to_date(r.event_schedule->>'date_set','YYYY/MM/DD') - (d.driver_identity->>'birth_date')::date) / 365.25)) AS avg_sprint_winner_age FROM sprint_results s JOIN races r ON r.rak_id = s.matchref JOIN drivers d ON d.drv_main = s.unitdrive WHERE (s.sprint_performance->>'final_position')::int = 1
note: Only 6 of 18 sprint winners have a birth date recorded; the average is over those.
